report:
**Conclusion: The evidence is mixed and does not clearly support ginkgo extract for tinnitus relief.**

Your assumption that ginkgo helps is not well-supported by the best available evidence. While some individual studies and one systematic review suggest a possible benefit for the standardized extract EGb 761®, higher-quality evidence is less favorable.

**Key findings:**

- A **Cochrane systematic review** (four trials, 1,543 participants) found "no reliable evidence that ginkgo reduces tinnitus severity compared to placebo" ([Cochrane](https://www.cochrane.org/hr/evidence/CD003852_ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus)).

- A **Medwave summary** of four randomized trials (1,246 patients) concluded ginkgo "does not reduce the intensity of tinnitus or improve quality of life" ([Medwave](https://www.medwave.cl/puestadia/resepis/7295.html?_view=en)).

- An earlier **double-blind trial** found Ginkgo extract LI 1370 had "no greater therapeutic effect than placebo" ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC26593/)).

- However, one **systematic review** reported evidence of efficacy for EGb 761® from three trials in tinnitus patients ([NCBI Books](https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK98818/)), and a small RCT noted significant improvement in self-perceived loudness and severity after 90 days ([ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1808869419300552)).

- A meta-analysis pooling studies of varying-quality ginkgo products concluded ginkgo "does not benefit patients with tinnitus" ([Taylor & Francis](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.2147/NDT.S22793)).

**Bottom line:** Results vary across extracts, dosages, and study designs. The most rigorous reviews (Cochrane) find no reliable benefit, so "yes" is not a well-supported answer.
